G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd
BRANCH MANAGER
Role · KRAs · KPIs · SOP · Consequences
Reports to: Regional Head  ·  Peer with: Senior Doctor (branch)

1  ·  Role Purpose
The Branch Manager owns the entire branch — revenue and operations together. The BM is not a supervisor of a clinic, but the owner of one. Every revenue rupee that comes in, every client experience that goes out, every team member's day-to-day discipline — all of it sits with the BM.

In one sentence.  Run the branch as if it were yours. Grow it. Hold it to standard. Build a team that does not need you to run it well.

The peer relationship with the doctor.  This is the structural decision most BMs get wrong. The senior doctor leads clinical. The BM leads everything else. Neither reports to the other. The two meet daily — not to coordinate as boss-and-subordinate but as equals running parallel functions inside the same branch. Minutes of every daily meeting go to corporate — Regional Head, Manisha, and Dr Kanikta (Head of Clinical at company level). The branches where the BM tries to manage the doctor, or where the doctor tries to manage the BM, are the branches that quietly fall apart.

2  ·  Key Result Areas (KRAs)
Six KRAs. Each carries weight in monthly review.
KRA 1 — Branch Revenue
Branch monthly revenue meets or exceeds target
Counsellor team converting at target rates — conversion to package, total revenue, overall conversion, upsell/cross-sell
Active balance recovery — outstanding dues collected before they age
New client acquisition and lapsed client win-back trending positively

KRA 2 — Branch Operations Quality
Every function meets daily standard — reception, counsellors, therapists, housekeeping
Compliance audit scores from Saurabh / Arshpreet consistently at or above standard
NPS / client feedback above target
Complaint rate per 100 visits below threshold; resolution within 24h SLA

KRA 3 — Doctor Coordination
Daily meeting with senior doctor held every working day — no exceptions
MoM filed same day to Regional Head, Manisha, and Dr Kanikta
Operational issues raised by doctor closed within agreed SLA
Client clinical issues escalated correctly — never overridden by BM operational decisions

KRA 4 — Team Development
Every direct report has a current performance scorecard
Underperformers on documented improvement plans, not protected
At least one Assistant BM identified and developing (succession plan)
Team attrition below company average

KRA 5 — Growth Planning
Monthly Branch Growth Plan submitted to Regional Head on schedule
Each month's plan more specific and ambitious than the last — branch grows quarter on quarter
Issues from last month either closed or moved to action with date and owner
Branch open asks (from team, from clients) addressed within agreed SLA

KRA 6 — Brand Stewardship
Zero hard-line violations in the branch — off-system payments, outcome guarantees, floor-breach pricing, fake conversions
Any reputational risk escalated to RH and founder same day
Clinical protocols followed across all departments — verified through audits

4  ·  Standard Operating Procedure
Every working day follows this rhythm. The discipline is what makes the branch run, not heroics.
Morning  ·  Before clients arrive
Floor walk — reception, cabins, washrooms, refreshment area. Look at the branch as a client would.
Reception huddle (5 min) — yesterday's score, today's appointments, VIPs, risks.
Housekeeping huddle (5 min) — same-day standards, asks from yesterday.
Counsellor huddle (10 min) — yesterday's follow-up list, today's expected consults, worried-about clients.
Daily meeting with senior doctor (15-30 min) — described separately below.

The daily BM-Doctor meeting — peer alignment
This is the single most important meeting of your day. Held every working day. Peers, not boss-subordinate. Minutes filed to corporate.

Agenda
Target review — where the branch stands on revenue and clinical delivery this week
Client challenges — any specific clients with issues, complications, complaints, concerns
Operational issues — anything in the branch that is blocking clinical work
Clinical issues — anything from clinical that affects operations
Growth plan progress — what is working, what needs to change
One thing each — one ask the BM has for the doctor, one ask the doctor has for the BM

MoM filing — same day
MoM drafted by the BM, reviewed by the doctor, agreed in writing
Filed to: Regional Head, Manisha, Dr Kanikta (Head of Clinical)
Format: short. Six headings (one per agenda item). One action per item with owner and date.

Why MoM matters.  Without the MoM, the daily meeting becomes a chat. With the MoM, it becomes a contract. The MoM goes to three senior people at corporate, which means both the BM and the doctor know what they agreed cannot quietly disappear. This is what makes peer relationships hold over time — not chemistry, but contractual visibility.

Through the day
Live verification of counsellor consultations — observe at least 2 per day
CRM audit — at least 5 records from yesterday, looking for missing follow-ups, inflated promises, undocumented details
Floor walks — every 2 hours, brief, visible to the team
Asks register check — anything raised by any team member, status updated
Doctor coordination — quick check-ins through the day on anything that came up

Evening  ·  After clients leave
Counsellor debrief at 6 PM — 15 min. Six questions every evening (in the daily log).
Receive Arshpreet / compliance findings if visited that day
Update daily log — KPIs, sentiment, open issues
Daily WhatsApp summary to Regional Head — 5 lines. Numbers, one story, one worry, one ask.
Plan tomorrow — confirmed bookings, follow-ups, any concerns from today carrying over.

5  ·  Monthly Rhythm  ·  Branch Growth Plan
The Branch Growth Plan is what separates a BM who runs the branch from a BM who builds it. Submitted monthly to the Regional Head. Reviewed in the monthly business review.
What the Branch Growth Plan covers
Last month's performance — KPIs vs target, what worked, what didn't
This month's commitment — specific revenue and operations targets, owner-level
Top 3 issues to eradicate — specific problems with owner, due date, success criteria
Top 3 growth bets — specific actions you are taking to grow the branch (new initiatives, team development, client retention plays)
Team development update — who is being coached on what, who is being prepared for a bigger role
Asks of corporate — anything you need from RH, Manisha, Saurabh, or founder to deliver this month's plan

The plan, not the report.  Most monthly submissions in this industry are reports — what happened last month. The Branch Growth Plan is the opposite — what will happen next month. The past month is one section out of six. The other five are forward-looking. This is by design.

6  ·  Authority and Escalation
What the BM decides without escalation
Day-to-day branch operations and team scheduling
Counsellor / reception / housekeeping scorecards and corrective coaching
Discount approvals up to authorised threshold
Client complaint resolution within 24h SLA
Operational spend within branch budget

What needs Regional Head sign-off
Hiring or terminating any team member
Discount above authorised threshold
Budget variance beyond agreed limits
Branch-level operational changes affecting more than one function
Disagreements with the senior doctor that cannot be resolved between you

What needs Manisha / Saurabh sign-off
Sales policy questions — what the brand allows, what it doesn't (Manisha)
Compliance issues that span branches (Saurabh)
Major SOP changes or exceptions

What comes to Harman / Founder directly
Pressure from anyone to break a hard-line violation
Serious client complaint with reputational risk
Regulatory or legal issue
Loss of a key senior person — senior doctor, top counsellor
Anything that feels structurally wrong

7  ·  Don'ts
Behaviours that are not acceptable, regardless of branch performance.

Treating the senior doctor as a subordinate — peer relationship is non-negotiable
Skipping the daily BM-Doctor meeting or filing MoM late
Protecting a counsellor or other team member who is failing because of personal loyalty
Having favourites — a preferred function or person who gets softer reviews
Allowing or directing any hard-line violation — off-system payments, outcome guarantees, fake conversions, floor-breach pricing
Hiding problems from the Regional Head
Bypassing the Regional Head to talk to Manisha, Saurabh, Harman, or founder on routine matters
Promising clients or team members anything not agreed with the RH
Treating company decisions as suggestions

8  ·  Consequences Framework
Trigger
Response
Single-month miss on a KPI
Documented in 1-on-1 with RH; cause analysis; corrective plan agreed
Two consecutive months miss on the same KPI
Written notice; 30-day improvement plan with weekly check-ins
Three consecutive months miss
Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with HR + RH + Manisha
Single hard-line violation in the branch (BM allowed or directed)
Same-day review; termination consideration
Daily BM-Doctor meeting skipped repeatedly
Written warning
MoM not filed on time, repeatedly
Written warning
Pattern of skipping growth plan submissions
Performance issue raised in next review
Serious dishonesty with RH or Founder
Single-incident termination consideration

9  ·  What 'Good' Looks Like — End of First Year

Branch revenue meets or exceeds target every month.
Compliance audit scores consistently at standard.
Daily BM-Doctor meeting happens without fail. MoMs go to corporate without delay.
Team is stable — counsellors converting, reception holding the standard, housekeeping clean.
Monthly Branch Growth Plan submitted on time, more ambitious quarter on quarter.
Founder or RH visits unannounced and finds the branch running well — not better than usual, just normally well.

The ultimate test.  A great BM is the BM whose branch keeps running well even when she takes a week off. That is not magic — it is systems, team development, and discipline held every day for months. Build for that horizon, and the rest follows.
